note: Candidate position summaries merged into data/races.json at page load (fills candidates with no summary). Short neutral paraphrases of candidates' campaign Issues/priorities pages and published candidate-comparison/voter-guide coverage; each links its source. Ballotpedia profiles could not be machine-read (bot protection).

AL.name: Barry Moore
AL.summary: Tax cuts for working families and small businesses (no tax on tips, overtime, Social Security); zero-tolerance illegal-immigration stance with permanent border security and deportations; anti-abortion; strong Second Amendment defender.

AL.name: Everett Wess
AL.summary: Campaigns on voting rights, reproductive freedom, economic opportunity and equal justice; supports keeping a federal Department of Education for grants and student loans.

AL.name: Tommy Tuberville
AL.summary: Lower taxes and less regulation to attract manufacturing; all-of-the-above energy (oil, gas, nuclear); anti-abortion; hardline border enforcement; school choice; has backed repealing the ACA.

AL.name: Doug Jones
AL.summary: Affordability platform: eliminate the grocery tax and suspend the gas tax when prices spike; Medicaid expansion; protect contraception and IVF access; free community college for adults without credentials; past support for universal background checks.

AK.name: Bernadette Wilson
AK.summary: Says Alaska has a spending, not revenue, problem; opposes raising oil taxes; restore the statutory PFD; push AKLNG and other resource projects; school choice; sponsor of the ranked-choice-voting repeal initiative.

AK.name: Dave Bronson
AK.summary: Resource-led growth (oil, gas incl. AKLNG, mining, timber) and less red tape; opposes changing oil taxes; full statutory PFD; school choice and parents' rights; supports pregnancy-resource and adoption services; strong gun-rights record.

AK.name: Treg Taylor
AK.summary: Responsible resource development and permitting reform, including Cook Inlet gas and AKLNG; no new taxes, balanced budgets and protecting the PFD; public safety and Second Amendment; end seabed-damaging trawling; reading proficiency and vocational education.

AR.name: Tom Cotton
AR.summary: Opposes the Green New Deal and climate mandates as costly; proof of citizenship to register and voter ID (SAVE America Act); co-sponsored the Dismantle DEI Act; U.S. AI leadership over China; highlights defense jobs in Arkansas.

AR.name: Hallie Shoffner
AR.summary: Lower costs for families (groceries, child care, housing, health care); protect rural hospitals and lower drug prices; help farmers adapt to climate change via Farm Bill incentives; would vote to defund ICE in its current form; supports 2A plus gun-safety laws.

AR.name: Sarah Huckabee Sanders
AR.summary: Arkansas National Guard assisting ICE enforcement; strong Second Amendment supporter; AI working group for safe state use; rural development ('Capital for a Day'); runs on her first-term record.

AR.name: Fredrick Love
AR.summary: Health care as a right and protecting Arkansas' Medicaid expansion (ARHOME); small-business, workforce and infrastructure investment; would halt state Education Freedom Account vouchers by executive order; supports abortion rights; wary of data-center growth.

CA.name: Xavier Becerra
CA.summary: Protect health coverage from federal cuts and move toward universal access; affordability focus (insurance, child care, groceries); affordable, reliable clean-energy transition; protect abortion access; defend immigrants and Dreamers in court; enforce local housing obligations.

CA.name: Steve Hilton
CA.summary: No state income tax on the first $150K of earnings, halve the gas tax, cut regulation; repeal wind/solar mandates in favor of gas, nuclear and rooftop solar; end state-funded Medi-Cal for undocumented immigrants; overturn the sanctuary law; third-grade reading goal.

CO.name: John Hickenlooper
CO.summary: Defend and expand Inflation Reduction Act climate investments and grid modernization; says ICE should be overhauled or shut down; universal background checks, assault-weapons ban and red-flag laws; universal preschool and affordable child care.

CO.name: Mark Baisley
CO.summary: Cut federal taxes and regulations; 'energy dominance' via expanded domestic production and faster permitting; health-cost competition (association plans, HSAs, price transparency); legal, vetted immigration; sponsored a state Second Amendment Protection Act.

CO.name: Phil Weiser
CO.summary: 'Healthy Colorado Plan' stressing primary/preventive care and lower costs; business formation and good jobs; meet emissions goals with solar, wind, storage and geothermal; protect reproductive rights; limit state cooperation with ICE; more K-12 funding and teacher pay.

CO.name: Victor Marx
CO.summary: Affordability and accountability on housing, energy, taxes and fees; end sanctuary policies and require cooperation with ICE; anti-abortion; strong Second Amendment supporter; 'clean, pragmatic energy' and stewardship of land and water; more affordable child care.

CT.name: Ned Lamont
CT.summary: Affordability: lower child-care, health, housing and energy costs; 100% zero-carbon grid by 2040; protect abortion providers and patients; protections for immigrant communities; gun-violence-prevention laws; expand universal pre-K and free school meals.

CT.name: Ryan Fazio
CT.summary: Cut costs and taxes, restore fiscal guardrails and pay down debt and pensions; lower electric bills by shifting public-benefit charges off utility bills; supports keeping abortion legal; reduce state spending on undocumented immigrants; end charter/magnet school lotteries.

DE.name: Chris Coons
DE.summary: Small-business growth, apprenticeships, affordable housing and infrastructure; clean-energy expansion; reproductive freedom including abortion and IVF; comprehensive immigration reform with border security; secure-storage and background-check gun laws; Pell Grant support.

DE.name: Michael Katz
DE.summary: Fiscal discipline to fight inflation, permanent pro-growth tax cuts; lower drug prices and fund rural health in Kent and Sussex; diversified energy including nuclear; border security and strong immigration enforcement; expand early-childhood education.

HI.name: Josh Green
HI.summary: Diversify the economy beyond tourism; aggressive climate action and clean-energy goals; supports abortion rights (signed 2023 access expansion); signed 2026 immigrant due-process protections; firearm-safety limits that he says respect the Second Amendment.

HI.name: Gary Cordery
HI.summary: Shrink taxes, fees and government; end the General Excise Tax on food and medicine and freeze primary-residence property taxes; critical of the state 'green fee'; practical, culturally grounded education with financial literacy; says abortion policy should follow the voters.

ID.name: Jim Risch
ID.summary: Energy independence led by expanded nuclear power and hydropower relicensing reform; federal education support that preserves local control; long Senate record on foreign relations.

ID.name: Todd Achilles
ID.summary: Independent: more border-patrol resources plus Idaho-first agricultural worker policies; protect public lands and the Roadless Rule; supports the Second Amendment with training emphasis; defend and strengthen public schools.

ID.name: Brad Little
ID.summary: Tax relief, deregulation and balanced budgets; signed Idaho's near-total abortion restrictions; cooperation with federal immigration enforcement; strengthened state firearms preemption; public schools, literacy and parent partnerships.

ID.name: Terri Pickens
ID.summary: Small-business-focused growth and family-centered budgets; protect public lands, rivers and wildlife; abortion, contraception and IVF decisions left to patients and doctors; supports the Second Amendment; higher teacher pay, rural school funding and universal pre-K.

IL.name: Juliana Stratton
IL.summary: Build on the Pritzker record: $15 federal minimum wage and expanded EITC; clean, reliable, affordable energy; strong reproductive-rights advocate; comprehensive immigration reform and has called for abolishing ICE.

IL.name: Don Tracy
IL.summary: Lower living costs by cutting taxes, spending, waste and fraud; health-price transparency and competition; all-of-the-above energy; calls abortion a state issue; secure the border and no taxpayer benefits for non-citizens, with a lawful path for workers; parents' rights.

IL.name: JB Pritzker
IL.summary: Raise wages, support small business and infrastructure; clean-energy transition under CEJA; protect and expand abortion access; defends the state assault-weapons ban; more school funding, early-childhood education and higher teacher minimum pay.

IL.name: Darren Bailey
IL.summary: Make Illinois affordable by lowering taxes and cutting wasteful spending; promote small business and jobs; energy framed around affordability, grid capacity and data-center rules; pro-life; campaign issues page centers on education, public safety and taxes.

KY.name: Andy Barr
KY.summary: Broad tax cuts including the 2025 law's tips/overtime/Social Security provisions; expand coal and other fossil-fuel production with faster permitting; defend Second Amendment rights; school choice and career/technical education.

KY.name: Charles Booker
KY.summary: Workers-first agenda: union jobs, living wages and rural public investment; moratorium on new hyperscale data centers pending safeguards; supports abortion access; would replace ICE with a due-process-centered system; treats gun violence as a public-health crisis; fully fund public schools.

LA.name: Julia Letlow
LA.summary: Lower taxes and regulation and make the Trump tax cuts permanent; expand oil, gas and LNG exports; lower health costs, close rural care gaps and cut Medicaid waste and fraud.

LA.name: Jamie Davis
LA.summary: Rural jobs and lower living costs; opposes carbon-capture pipelines that use eminent domain; secure border plus a fair legal-immigration process; modernized public schools with more trade-school options.

ME.name: Hannah Pingree
ME.summary: Universal, affordable health care with a state-backed public option; lower household costs plus apprenticeships and job training; clean energy with utility accountability; enshrine abortion rights in the state constitution; supports limits on cooperation with ICE; gun-safety endorsed; fund public schools.

ME.name: Robert (Bobby) Charles
ME.summary: Abolish the state income tax, cut regulation and spending; restore reliable, affordable power; 'unapologetically pro-life'; backs federal immigration enforcement; defends gun owners while prosecuting crime; schools refocused on reading, math and science with curriculum transparency.

ME.name: Rick Bennett
ME.summary: Independent: pursue universal health care under Maine's 2021 framework; speed up housing permits and expand factory-built homes; energy affordability and local control; supports abortion rights; strong Second Amendment supporter; early reading/math screening and intervention.

MD.name: Wes Moore
MD.summary: 'Work, wages and wealth' via life sciences, tech, AI and cyber investment; clean energy with affordability and reliability; protect and expand abortion access; cooperate with ICE on violent offenders but oppose broad sweeps; gun-violence prevention; record K-12 funding and Blueprint implementation.

MD.name: Dan Cox
MD.summary: Cut taxes and fees, cap property-tax assessments and reduce permitting costs; bring power plants back online and pursue small modular reactors; pro-life; opposes public-health mandates; fully fund schools with dollars directed to classrooms.

MA.name: Ed Markey
MA.summary: Lower costs via housing, nutrition and energy aid; bold climate action and clean-energy investment (Green New Deal co-author); codify Roe; pathway to citizenship; assault-weapons ban and stronger background checks; universal pre-K and affordable college.

MA.name: John Deaton
MA.summary: Cut federal waste and balance the budget; lower drug prices and rein in pharmacy benefit managers; acknowledges climate risk to coastal states but opposes the Green New Deal; targeted state-federal cooperation to deport serious criminals.

MA.name: Maura Healey
MA.summary: Lower business costs and attract investment; clean-energy expansion with affordability and reliability; signed 2026 laws expanding abortion access and limiting immigration enforcement in sensitive locations; stricter firearm laws; early-literacy investment.

MA.name: Mike Minogue
MA.summary: Cut taxes, spending and unfunded mandates; lower energy costs including via gas pipelines; 'Patients First' health-access plan; pro-life but would uphold existing state abortion law; oppose sanctuary status and deport criminal undocumented immigrants; opt into federal school-choice tax credits.

MN.name: Amy Klobuchar
MN.summary: Lower health premiums through stronger reinsurance and MNsure credits; lower household costs and expand job pathways; grid modernization and affordable renewables; protect reproductive freedom; immigration reform including farm-worker visas; evidence-based reading/math and tutoring.

MN.name: Lisa Demuth
MN.summary: Find $1B in state-agency savings mainly by targeting fraud; all-of-the-above energy and repeal of Minnesota's nuclear moratorium; restrictive abortion record; opposed semiautomatic-weapons and magazine bans; 'dramatic reset' for schools focused on reading proficiency.

MS.name: Cindy Hyde-Smith
MS.summary: Supports domestic oil, gas, nuclear and biofuel production and warns against foreign energy dependence; runs on her conservative Senate record and agriculture work.

MS.name: Scott Colom
MS.summary: Invest in good-paying jobs and education; raise the federal minimum wage; end federal income taxes for teachers and police officers.

MS.name: Ty Pinkins
MS.summary: Independent: 'pro-woman' on abortion (personal decisions belong to women); orderly, humane immigration with modern ports of entry and faster asylum processing; gun ownership for law-abiding citizens plus measures like higher minimum ages; resilient infrastructure and sustainable farming.

MT.name: Kurt Alme
MT.summary: Affordability through balanced budgets, less deficit spending and tax relief; more housing by cutting construction red tape; public safety: secure border, back law enforcement, prosecute violent crime and drug cartels, plus prevention and treatment; rural health via the Rural Health Transformation Program, telehealth and price transparency.

MT.name: Alani Bankhead
MT.summary: Stepwise path to universal health care (Medicaid for All, then Medicare for All); no data centers on public lands without verified environmental protections; immigration reform with expanded legal pathways; replace crumbling schools and fund vocational paths.

MT.name: Seth Bodnar
MT.summary: Independent: make Montana more affordable by lowering housing and health-care costs and reforming prescription-drug pricing.

NE.name: Jim Pillen
NE.summary: Pro-business, fiscally conservative growth with targeted incentives and limits on public costs and regulation; expand energy production while protecting public power; pro-life; stronger immigration enforcement with federal cooperation; signed constitutional carry; K-12 focus on academics, parental choice and trades.

NE.name: Lynne Walz
NE.summary: Health care as an economic-development and workforce strategy; growth via manufacturing, broadband, agriculture and Main Street businesses; says government should stay out of personal health decisions; voted against permitless carry; invest in public schools.

NH.name: Kelly Ayotte
NH.summary: No income or sales tax and a low-tax business climate; more housing through less regulation; advanced nuclear power roadmap; keep current abortion law and veto new restrictions; limit sanctuary policies; expanded gun-rights laws; public schools plus Education Freedom Accounts.

NH.name: Cinde Warmington
NH.summary: Affordability: suspend the gas tax, statewide housing plan and fund; opposes sales and income taxes; expand health access and criticizes Medicaid premium increases; clean energy; repeal abortion limits; gun-safety rules (waiting period, red flag); repeal EFA vouchers, expand pre-K.

NJ.name: Cory Booker
NJ.summary: Raise wages and benefits, support entrepreneurship and lower housing costs; codify Roe and expand reproductive-health access; educational equity so zip code doesn't decide opportunity.

NJ.name: Justin Murphy
NJ.summary: Pro-growth tax relief including abolishing the IRS and replacing the tax code; school choice and local control (vouchers, tax credits, charters, homeschooling).

NM.name: Ben Ray Luján
NM.summary: Climate action and environmental justice (led law to plug abandoned oil and gas wells); federal abortion protections; comprehensive immigration reform; bipartisan gun-safety framework; early-childhood and Head-Start-through-college education investment.

NM.name: Larry Marker
NM.summary: Pro-growth, market-friendly policy defending energy independence and New Mexico energy jobs; opposes federal overreach and permitting delays; total border security to curb fentanyl and cartels.

NM.name: Deb Haaland
NM.summary: Diversify the economy beyond federal and oil-and-gas revenue with small-business support; renewable transition and net-zero by 2050; protect abortion access; limit ICE use of state resources and bar masked agents; gun-safety measures plus illegal-gun enforcement; early literacy and universal child care.

NM.name: Gregg Hull
NM.summary: Diversify the economy via research commercialization and advanced manufacturing; all-of-the-above energy including more oil and gas; stabilize rural hospitals and expand telehealth; pro-life, opposes state funding of abortion for out-of-state patients; strong 2A; tie school funding to measurable results.

NY.name: Kathy Hochul
NY.summary: Job-linked training for high-demand industries; climate-resilient infrastructure; protect and expand abortion access including medication abortion; limit state role in civil immigration enforcement except for serious crimes; stronger gun-safety laws; universal child care and expanded education access.

NY.name: Bruce Blakeman
NY.summary: Lower taxes and cut fraud and waste; sharply reduce Medicaid spending; scrap the state climate law (CLCPA); local cooperation with ICE and repeal of the 287(g) ban; calls himself pro-choice; gun owner backing 'reasonable restrictions'; school choice.

OK.name: Kevin Hern
OK.summary: All-of-the-above domestic energy and streamlined permitting; pro-life; border security with full ICE/CBP funding; Second Amendment defender (concealed-carry reciprocity); expand 529 plans to K-12, homeschool and workforce credentials.

OK.name: N'Kiyla Thomas
OK.summary: Health care as a right: protect and expand the ACA and rural OB-GYN access; environmental protection as public health; restore Roe federally; smaller class sizes, early intervention and less reliance on testing.

OK.name: Mike Mazzei
OK.summary: Phase out the state income tax over six years and cut regulation; opposes abortion in all circumstances; expanded 287(g) cooperation with ICE; statewide literacy director and classroom accountability.

OK.name: Cyndi Munson
OK.summary: Protect Medicaid and rural maternity care; paid family leave and workforce investment; all-of-the-above energy; ask voters to overturn the abortion ban; due process for immigrants; 2A plus child gun-safety measures; fully fund schools and repeal the private-school tax-credit voucher.

OR.name: Jeff Merkley
OR.summary: Runs on his Senate record; co-sponsored the Algorithmic Accountability Act on AI in housing, jobs and schools; focuses on Oregon wildfire and smoke as a public-health emergency.

OR.name: David Brock Smith
OR.summary: No new taxes, cut fraud and red tape, support local business; criticizes Oregon climate laws as raising costs; opposes expanding abortion access; stronger border enforcement and ICE coordination; NRA-endorsed; expand mental-health services.

OR.name: Tina Kotek
OR.summary: Business growth, faster permitting and a new commerce department; more housing and child care; defend Oregon Health Plan against federal cuts; clean-energy transition; protect abortion access; limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement; stricter gun laws; early literacy.

OR.name: Christine Drazan
OR.summary: Day-one affordability order and repeal of Kotek's climate executive order; veto tax and fee hikes, reform the Corporate Activity Tax, protect the kicker; audit homelessness spending and fund state police; pro-life; local cooperation with ICE; school choice and parental authority.

PA.name: Josh Shapiro
PA.summary: Lower costs, cut red tape and attract private investment; Pennsylvania-specific clean-energy and permitting approach; generally pro-immigrant guidance during enforcement operations; more public-school funding, career/technical education and college affordability.

PA.name: Stacy Garrity
PA.summary: 'Turn Around PA': expand energy production, lift limits on new drilling and speed permits for gas, pipelines and power plants; cut taxes and expand property-tax rebates; expand school choice (Lifeline Scholarships, tax-credit scholarships).

RI.name: Jack Reed
RI.summary: Limit carbon pollution and expand clean energy; supports abortion rights and federal protections; comprehensive immigration reform with border security and an earned path to citizenship; improved background checks and anti-trafficking gun measures.

RI.name: Raymond McKay
RI.summary: Lower heating, electric and food costs and attract business investment; shore up Medicare by trimming programs; energy independence with nuclear and fossil fuels; no taxpayer funds for abortion providers; secure borders and 'responsible' immigration; school choice.

RI.name: Helena Foulkes
RI.summary: Remove barriers for businesses and make it easier to start one; tackle energy costs and climate together with cheaper renewables; supports abortion rights; opposes 287(g) police-ICE agreements; ban assault-weapon and high-capacity magazine sales; $100M bond for career/technical school facilities.

RI.name: Aaron Guckian
RI.summary: 'Rhode Island Works Smarter' plan to cut spending and improve efficiency; all-of-the-above energy and review of climate mandates; health-care access and affordability; supports charter schools and school choice.

SC.name: Darline Graham Nordone
SC.summary: Strongly pro-life; hard-line on illegal immigration, including deportation; strong Second Amendment supporter.

SC.name: Annie Andrews
SC.summary: Health care as a right: public option, protect Medicaid/Medicare, lower drug costs, mental-health access, keep rural hospitals open; end tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy and raise wages; abortion decisions left to women and families; border security with a fair path to citizenship; 2A plus universal background checks; fully fund public schools.

SC.name: Alan Wilson
SC.summary: Eliminate the state income tax and cut property taxes for seniors; opposes federal climate and ESG mandates; firmly pro-life; strong state immigration enforcement and no benefits for undocumented residents; defends 2A; fully fund schools while expanding school choice and early literacy.

SC.name: Jermaine Johnson
SC.summary: Income-tax relief so most families pay no state income tax; worker-focused growth; at least 25% in-state energy production for resilience; supports enforcement but opposes current ICE operations as conducted; full K-12 public-education audit.

SD.name: Mike Rounds
SD.summary: Pro-growth, low-tax, less-regulation economy; all-of-the-above energy independence; introduced the Life at Conception Act.

SD.name: Brian Bengs
SD.summary: Independent: overhaul health care to cut costs and widen access; maintain and strengthen environmental regulation; education as a tool against intergenerational poverty, with attention to school-funding disparities.

SD.name: Larry Rhoden
SD.summary: Targeted economic development via state Future and REDI funds; property rights and limits on eminent domain for CO2 pipelines; strongly anti-abortion; expanded Highway Patrol cooperation with ICE; shift education control from Washington to the state and localities.

SD.name: Dan Ahlers
SD.summary: Affordable care statewide and keep rural hospitals open; redirect economic-development money to small businesses; protect landowner rights on CO2 pipelines; supports abortion rights record; recruit and retain teachers, strengthen rural schools and early-childhood education.

TN.name: Bill Hagerty
TN.summary: Tax and spending restraint, deregulation and more housing supply; expand energy production and LNG exports; pro-life, states regulate abortion; stronger border and immigration enforcement; opposes new gun restrictions.

TN.name: Marquita Bradshaw
TN.summary: Affordable health care for all; environmental and climate justice (clean air, safe water, clean energy); codify Roe; DACA protections and a path to citizenship; universal background checks.

TN.name: Marsha Blackburn
TN.summary: Keep taxes low and cut spending and regulation to attract jobs; '100 percent pro-life'; enforce immigration law and oppose sanctuary policies; gun owner who defends 2A; extend Education Freedom Scholarships to all families.

TN.name: Jerri Green
TN.summary: End the grocery tax and shift it to corporations; expand Medicaid and protect rural hospitals and TennCare; protect public lands and clean air/water; repeal the near-total abortion ban; end state-local cooperation with ICE; universal background checks; fully fund public schools instead of vouchers.

VT.name: Phil Scott
VT.summary: Affordability and restrained spending with business and infrastructure investment; energy affordability including nuclear in the clean mix; supports abortion rights (signed 2019 protections); legal, compassionate immigration; school-system restructuring under 2026 reform law.

VT.name: Amanda Janoo
VT.summary: Begin universal health care with universal primary and preventive care; bottom-up economy built on local businesses, farmers and co-ops; community-owned renewable energy; reproductive freedom; critical of ICE activity in Vermont; protect small schools.

VA.name: Mark Warner
VA.summary: Fairer tax code, affordable health care and an innovation agenda for the middle class; defend clean-energy and advanced-manufacturing investments; restore abortion rights (Women's Health Protection Act); universal background checks and an assault-weapons ban; ease student debt.

VA.name: Bert Mizusawa
VA.summary: Fiscal responsibility and balancing the budget; lower health costs, hold insurers accountable and fund rural hospitals; secure borders while making legal immigration easier; pro-life.

WV.name: Shelley Moore Capito
WV.summary: Tax relief, small business and infrastructure investment; all-of-the-above energy centered on coal, oil and gas; pro-life voting record; more funding for border security and immigration enforcement; education and workforce training from early childhood up.

WV.name: Rachel Fetty Anderson
WV.summary: Medicare/Medicaid/Tricare-for-all style coverage; fair pay, safe workplaces and the right to unionize; invest in solar, wind and hydro while keeping coal in the mix; invest in children's education, health and welfare.

WY.name: Harriet Hageman
WY.summary: Cut federal spending to fight inflation and limit government; expand oil, gas, coal and critical-mineral production; strengthen rural health care; life begins at conception; strict border enforcement as a top priority.

WY.name: James Byrd
WY.summary: Diversify Wyoming beyond volatile fossil-fuel markets while protecting energy workers; permitting reform; renewables and advanced nuclear alongside fossil fuels; secure the border and enforce the law but oppose family separation; responsible, locked gun storage; rural education.

WY.name: Eric Barlow
WY.summary: Strengthen core industries (energy and minerals, agriculture, tourism); expand coal, oil, gas, uranium and nuclear; firmly pro-life with maternal-health support; no state money for undocumented immigrants; strong 2A defender; local control of schools with parental involvement.

WY.name: Kenneth Casner
WY.summary: Says Wyoming is 'ruled by the outside,' with wealth flowing to investors and extraction companies; would run an 'open-door' governor's office that documents and investigates residents' concerns.
